text: Whether a fetch to http://[::ffff:7f00:1]/ actually reaches IPv4 loopback on a deploy host (critic-01). It depends on dual-stack mapping (net.ipv6.bindv6only) and needs a listener, which the no-port rule excludes. Only the guard's verdict was observed.

The umask and service manager on real installs. They decide whether critic-03's log and database files are group- or world-readable, and whether a systemd journal also keeps the token line. The repo does not show them.
How operators actually deploy: behind a reverse proxy or bound directly. critic-02's choice between trusting X-Forwarded-For and using one shared bucket depends on it, and the repo cannot show it.

Dependency vulnerabilities, outdated packages and licences: npm audit and npm outdated need the network, and NOTICE was not compared with dependency licences. npm ls lists 5 extraneous packages in the local node_modules (@emnapi/core, @emnapi/runtime, @emnapi/wasi-threads, @napi-rs/wasm-runtime, @tybys/wasm-util); they were not traced against package-lock.json.
A secret scan of git history: gitleaks was not run, and tooling-29 records that its config skips tests/.
Bundle size, and whether a script-src CSP can work with Next's inline scripts. Both need next build.
Session-cookie design: the cookie value is the raw token with a one-year maxAge (src/proxy.ts:285-291). Read, but not assessed as a finding.

The cycle scanner parses imports by regex, so a re-export without a from clause or a string-built path could hide a cycle. An eslint no-cycle or dependency-cruiser run would confirm the count of one real cycle.
Column-level dead data in SQLite (the lib-data gap) and LOCKBOOK.md's rulings against the code (the org gap) were not attempted. LOCKBOOK has 0 backticked repo paths to check mechanically.
Line-by-line reads of the 11 pages app listed, and visual equivalence for the components folds, remain open.
src/modules/hermes/components/PlatformsPanel.tsx (120 lines, 0 raw controls) and src/modules/hermes/handlers/profile-patch.ts (137 lines): measured only.

tests/integration/test_full_install_update_process.py (1,613 lines) and tests/scripts/run-shell-custom-tests.sh (554 lines): scanned only for API routes, script paths and alias names. No stale route or path was found (scripts/install.sh is the upstream Hermes installer URL, hindsight_bridge.py is a test fixture). Their logic was not read.

test-harness/ files other than the bench-gateway harness (baseline-fix-verify.mjs, poll-run.mjs, poll-pair.mjs, hermes-seed.Dockerfile, hermes-home/) were not read. Tooling reports 9 tooling files with zero references, and these may be among them.

Hindsight client hooks: the read path through hindsightGet inside effects is already in the hooks sceptic's note, and their writes all go through runWrite (grep). A conversion to useApiResource was not costed.

No jest, Playwright or coverage run, per the review rules. Suite durations come from the local jest perf-cache (2026-09-10T18:58Z) and coverage from the gitignored coverage/coverage-summary.json (2026-09-07). Both need a fresh run before any number is acted on.
The e2e total (about 276) is derived from static test() counts and loop sizes; npx playwright test --list was not run.
tests/integration/test_full_install_update_process.py (1,613 lines) and tests/scripts/run-shell-custom-tests.sh (554 lines): only their CI wiring was checked, not their content or duplication.
tests/e2e/lib/census-analysis.ts and census-collect.ts (873 lines) and their unit oracles (u0-census-arithmetic.test.ts, 461 lines): only imports were checked.
tests/helpers story.tsx, fixtures.ts, fetch-map.ts, render-with-query.tsx and page-subtitle.ts: adoption was counted; the code was not read line by line.
Of the 126 source-text suites, the 93 mixed ones were counted, not classified one by one; 8 of the 33 pure ones were classified from their headers.
Mock-conflict analysis for subject merges covered route-handler groups only. lib and component groups such as @/lib/db/sql-migrations (25 suites) and @/lib/composer/schema (22) were not analysed.
Whether the 47 whole-module api-auth mocks currently hide a real read-only defect was not tested; that needs the suites run with PS_READ_ONLY=1.
The code quality of mock-hermes, mock-hindsight, mock-llm and test-harness/ was not reviewed; only whether and where they run.
The two e2e flake hypotheses (a reused keep-alive socket; a re-press interrupting a force-dynamic navigation) come from reading the code and were not reproduced under load.

Did not run npm run lint, eslint over src, the jest suite, next build, Playwright, docker builds or CI (review rules). So per-step gate durations, the time saved by tooling-07 and tooling-15, and the violation counts for the two globally disabled react-hooks rules (tooling-28) are unmeasured.

Did not read the large script bodies line by line: ps-deploy.mjs (510), install.sh (446), setup-hindsight.sh (442), setup.sh (327), output-canary.mjs (748), design-lint.mjs (884), the docs pipeline (scripts/docs, 2,057 lines) and scripts/lib/*.sh (769). Duplication within them, and between setup.sh/install.sh and ps-deploy.mjs, was assessed only from headers and grep.
The three mock servers (mock-hermes, mock-llm, mock-hindsight) were not compared for shared HTTP-server boilerplate. Three consumers could justify a helper, but it was not measured.
Did not measure what widening knip's project to tests/ and test-harness/ would report (it needs a config change); tooling-16 flags that it will likely surface more.

tests/integration/test_full_install_update_process.py, tests/scripts/run-shell-custom-tests.sh and tests/scripts/boot-smoke.mjs belong to the tests dimension and were examined only where CI or package.json call them.
The Docker runtime image's content and size were not measured, including whether copying all of scripts/ into the runner stage (Dockerfile:46) is needed.
GitHub repository settings (branch protection, required checks) are not visible from the repo; tooling-30 relies on docs/contributing/testing.md:180 and ci.yml:422-425.
Did not verify whether hermes-registry-import.mjs stores provider key values or only references in the build-time repo-local database (tooling-13); only its header was read.
Did not check whether prerendered routes need a database at build time, which decides how much of tooling-13 is removable.
The Node 20 end-of-life date (2026-04-30) in tooling-04 comes from the published Node.js release schedule, not from anything in the repo.
Column-level dead-data analysis: only table names were matched against code; individual columns were not traced from writer to reader (for example sessions.provider, sync_registry.source_mtime).

Nothing was executed: no jest suite, no app run, no live database. The LogSync duplicate rows, the missing idx_runs_story on a v2 climb and the unreachable rebuild branch come from reading code and git history, not from observation.
Whether any live install carries schema_version > 103 or a database from before 2026-05-20 cannot be determined from the repository (lib-data-05).

Repository bodies checked only through grep metrics, not read line by line: composer, models, credentials, schedules, chat, deep-research, retention, agent-progression, analytics, stats/derive.ts, retention-prune.ts.
src/app/api/mission-categories/route.ts was not read, so how it uses getSchemaHealth's result is unverified (lib-data-23).
SyncScheduler.ts beyond its constants and method outline, and the hermes module's ConfigSync source (src/modules/hermes), were not reviewed.
Dockerfile and CI use of prebuild-db.mjs were not checked (lib-data-20).
The ADR record beyond the ADR-0004 and ADR-0009 references in code comments was not read for rulings on dropping tables.
src/lib/analytics/event-types.ts and categories.ts (taxonomies embedded in TypeScript) were not assessed for a move to JSON.
No rendering, Playwright run or design census. Visual-equivalence claims for the proposed folds (components-02, -08, -11, -12, -21, -31) are read from class strings, not pixels.
Did not run jest. Test impact comes from import and source-text scans (importers.json textRefs), not from executing suites.

About 45 of 204 files were read line by line. The rest were covered only by the scans (importers, labels, raw controls, toggles, plurals, comment paths, exports): PageHeader, SettingsSection, CategoryCombobox, CategoryManagerModal, ComposerRunForm, ComposerNodeRunDetail, WorkflowRunCanvas, ResearchReport, the Quest/Agent/Help/Log/Session/Script/Skill row and modal families, SegmentedControl, IconButton, LinkButton, Badge, EmptyState, Popover, SplitPane, button-chrome, the rest of DataList, the viz charts, motion/index.tsx, DeployControls, AchievementShowcase.
Whether ui/Badge supports an icon slot was not checked; it decides the StatusBadge fold in components-29.
The export scan is regex-based: namespace imports and exports re-exported through barrels may be misclassified (default re-exports through barrels were excluded).

Twenty regex hits for <button> without type= include comment matches (Card.tsx:31, GlowSurface.tsx:9, PerRowDeleteButton.tsx:29, RowActionButtons.tsx:19); HindsightBrowser.tsx:126, SessionFilterBar.tsx:66/78, ErrorBoundary.tsx:50 and SegmentedControl.tsx:103 were not opened, nor was whether any sits inside a <form>.
ConceptHint.tsx's hand-rolled listener was seen only by grep (line 55); its Escape handling was not read.
The census's repeated-window lines were attributed only for the four skills files; other component contributions to srcRepeatedWindowLines were not traced window by window.
src/kit/BloomField.tsx is a vendored, hash-pinned copy (src/kit/PROVENANCE.md, tests/unit/kit-provenance.test.ts); it was examined for scope only and no change is proposed.
scripts/tooling/design-lint.mjs and line-census.mjs are outside this scope; components-01 and components-29 describe their effect on components and leave the fix to the tooling reviewer.
CreateProfileModal and EditProfileModal (101/106 lines) were compared and not reported: two consumers, different state ownership, and a shared form would not pay for its interface.

Pages read only through AST and grep metrics, not line by line: work/composer, work/chat, agent/settings/restore, the dashboard page.tsx, results/insights, results/logs, results/sessions (list), work/scripts, work/research, agent/skills and agent/tools. The handler lists quoted for them come from grep extracts, not a full read.

Route files counted by grep but not read in full: config, credentials/[id], models/import, models/[id]/diff, monitor, logs, sessions (list), chat and chat/[id]/*, composer runs/*, laboratory/research/*, artifacts, skills toggle and [...path], agent/root, agent/profiles/[id] and sync/*, fs/*, analytics/timeseries, status, schedules/[id]/run.

No build, Playwright or jest run, per the review rules. app-08 (the layout ErrorBoundary is redundant) and app-15 (the two-hop redirect chain) are reasoned from the code and Next's segment conventions, not observed on a running instance. app-23 relies on the .next build artefact from 2026-09-10.

Orphan detection is literal and template-string search only. An endpoint assembled from a variable (a URL map, or a path fragment joined at runtime) would evade it, and external operator scripts or curl habits cannot be seen from the repo.
src/app/globals.css (808 lines) and the favicon: UI-overhaul scope, not examined here.
proxy.ts's inline 401 HTML page with hard-coded hex colours (#05080d, #0d1420, #eaf2f8) was not measured against the design tokens; it looks intentionally standalone.

Not checked: which tests pin the 400 sentences that app-18's zod conversions would change, and which tests assert log contexts for the seven routes in app-05 (beyond b1-sync-routes-answer-with-the-outcome.test.ts).
The Story Weaver reader settings that pick among the four serif fonts (src/modules/rec-room) sit outside this scope and were not measured for app-22.
Scratchpad measurement scripts (orphans.mjs, orphans2.mjs, pageshape.mjs) live in the session scratchpad only; a re-run needs them recreated from the methods above.

Nothing was run: no jest, build or app. The per-poll toasts (hooks-02), the stale dashboard cache entry (hooks-01) and the staggered /api/stats fetches (hooks-10) come from reading the code and TanStack's query-core source.
The exact number of unit suites that fail when the useToast fallback is removed (hooks-06) needs that change tried on a branch; only a grep upper bound (23) is given.

The client-side hooks under src/components/memory/hindsight/ (useHindsightCrudTab, useHindsightMemories, useHindsightModels, useHindsightDirectives) were only checked for their ShowToast type, not for their read and write paths.
TemplateEditorModal, MissionCreateForm and MissionsList bodies were not read, so the prop-reshape savings in hooks-07 and hooks-08 are estimates from the page's call sites.
The server modules in src/lib/api (api-auth, auth-token, auth-throttle, read-only, api-schemas, api-response) were reviewed for duplication and usage counts only, not for security correctness.
Converting the Story Weaver pages' 10 raw fetch calls is page-layer work; only the tooling gap is reported here.
Client reads and writes under src/modules/** (rec-room) were not examined.
src/lib/chat/chat-utils.ts was read only for its API wrappers and run-event handling, not for its markdown and export helpers.
Whether GitHub Actions is currently red on Linux because of the six case-mismatched links (docs-01). I did not query Actions or use gh.
Whether the 21 screenshots still match the current UI. Checking needs `npm run screenshots` (Playwright, binds a port), which the review rules exclude.
Output of `npm run docs:build`: not run, because it writes site/ and public/help/. The local site/ is gitignored and dated Sep 6, so I did not inspect it as current.

Read in full: docs/README.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, repo-guide.md, runtime-architecture.md, testing.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SUPPORT.md, getting-help.md, adr/README.md, REBRANDING.md and the branding READMEs. The other ~60 pages (the 21 guides, 20 concepts and most running/reference pages) were checked by script for paths, routes, env vars, identifiers, npm scripts and bold labels, plus targeted greps, not read line by line.
Behavioural claims in the guides (what a control does, counts such as '32 quests' or '~36 achievements') beyond label existence.
design-tokens.md token values against globals.css. Only names were checked: 25 named, 2 absent, both the page's intentional warning about --ch-* variables.
Content of the org/ pages the docs point to (org/START.md, org/EOS_OPERATORS_GUIDE.md, org/decisions/*); they exist but are outside this scope.
Legal adequacy of NOTICE, TRADEMARK.md and branding/LICENSE.md.
public/help/ output shape and the in-app Help resolver, apart from the one read path in src/lib/help/help-source.ts:97.

Bundle size was not measured. It needs `next build`, which this review may not run. Only static import checks were done (no zod or js-yaml in 'use client' files; @xyflow/react deferred via next/dynamic).
knip was not run (heavy on a shared machine), so the dead-export and unused-dependency claims come from grep.
tsc over scripts/**/*.ts was not run, so the number of latent type errors behind cross-cutting-09 and the caller errors behind apiFetch<T = unknown> are unknown.
No server or jest suite was run. The boot-line bug (cross-cutting-01) and the gateway mismatch (cross-cutting-02) come from reading the code.
The 242 catch blocks without an error binding were counted, not individually classified as intentional or swallowing.

Env reads in Python (tests/integration/*.py) and shell scripts were scanned with a ${VAR} regex only. Shell-internal variables such as PS_C_CYAN were not separated from operator config, and a regex cannot tell which shell names are exported.
Client-side error presentation (toasts, banners, inline error text) was not inventoried for duplicate spellings.
lib-to-modules imports (6 in 5 files) were not re-examined: ADR-0005 records them as measured exceptions, and the lib reviewer owns them.
org/decisions ADRs were not read in full, apart from ADR-0005's dependency rule. I did not confirm whether any ADR sets a lifetime for the rename aliases.
CSS token and class naming was out of scope; the UI programme U0-U20 covers it.
Docs and org content beyond environment-variable references were not reviewed; other dimensions cover them.
Did not read the full text of all 145 task records, the 7 reviews or the 4 plans. Records were measured by script, and plans and reviews by front matter, status sections and grep.
Did not verify the bodies of ADR-0001 to ADR-0006 and ADR-0009 against the code beyond the path-existence scan and the T-0144 diff.
Did not validate RULINGS.json, eos-session0/*.json or the task records against the EOS JSON schemas; that needs running python -m tools.eos from the sibling checkout, which this review did not do.
Did not run check-derived-views.mjs, check-doc-links.mjs or the c0/c8/u16/b15 jest suites to confirm they are green now; conclusions come from reading their source.
Did not check the LOCKBOOK.md body (360 lines; only the header and part of the Tokens section read) or its rulings against the code.
Did not confirm whether the EOS seed check accepts an org/ path in LOCKBOOK's rulings_record before proposing the change in org-07.
Did not inspect GitHub-side state (branch protection, remote branches beyond git branch -a) that bears on T-0003.
Did not review the user's auto-memory files outside the repository, although they restate HANDOVER content.
Did not assess EOS_FEEDBACK.md entries one by one for whether the estate resolved them after the pin, beyond the task views friction.

No jest, knip, build, Playwright or design-lint runs, per the review rules. The test-only export list comes from a word-boundary text search, so a string-built dynamic import or re-export chain could hide a user; all 19 candidates were spot-checked across the whole repo, including .mts files and org/.

Read only through census windows, importer counts and headers, not body by body: most of missions/ (30 files, 3,370 lines, including mission-repository.ts and mission-category-repository.ts), models/models-repository.ts, schedule/schedules-repository.ts, orchestration/run-reconcile.ts and scheduler/tick.ts, and the rec-room handlers create/edit/generate and components.
memory/ (Hindsight files and memory-providers), spend/, search/ internals, skills/, help/help-manifest.ts logic and schedule/ internals: importers and headers only.
runtime/state-db.ts and runtime/memory-db.ts were treated as the sanctioned Hermes port and not audited for naming or duplication.
No security review of fs/path-security.ts, search/url-guard.ts or the scripts-manager exec path beyond reading scripts-manager.ts.

Which unit suites assert on source text by regex was measured for only 8 files (chat-utils, config-schema, scripts-manager, profile-config-builder, engine, quest-defs, HermesRuntime, utils), so the refactor cost for the other files is unknown.

Other scopes (src/lib/api, db, seed, sessions, stats, sync, ui, analytics, dashboard, retention, schema; src/hooks; scripts/) were examined only where a finding crosses into them, e.g. hooks/useModels.ts, db/parse-json.ts, the ch-*.sh scripts.
